challenge.better_approach: Moving the shim's last_known under its folder would also stop the stray dir, but the resolver should not be sealable by any stray dir; the resolver change is one condition and covers both. The shim's split address is noted for its own ticket.
challenge.hidden_assumption: That a typed word matching a stray instance dir and an answers_as means the charter's device; a charter declaration is the authored name, a stray dir is runtime residue.
challenge.prior_art: f942a413f26d added the answers_as lookup with the instance-dir test; this narrows that test.
challenge.real_collision: None: 11.3.2 and 11.4.2 state the names; the change only makes them hold.

answers.falsifier: Done when (1) with stray instance-space dirs named inference and database, `cairn inference show` and `cairn database show` reach the bus mouth with argv [<typed name>, show] and never print 'no such device'; (2) a typed folder name (inferenceproxy) still resolves as itself and reaches the bus mouth with argv [inferenceproxy, show]; (3) a word that no folder carries and no charter declares still reads 'no such device or command' and never reaches the bus mouth.
answers.from_idea: none, because the defect is measured against outline 11.3.2 and 11.4.2 in cairn/devices/cairn/requirements/11-proxy-devices.md
answers.how: bin/cairn: the answers_as block's condition drops `&& ! -d "$INSTANCE_ROOT/$device"`, so the lookup runs whenever the class folder is absent. A word no charter declares is unchanged (the loop rewrites nothing). The proof runs bin/cairn as a subprocess over a scratch CAIRN_INSTANCE_ROOT from the scratch door, holding stray inference/0/last_known.json and database/0/last_known.json, with a stub CAIRN_BUS_MOUTH that records its argv, shaped like bin/proofs/test_a_word_with_no_script_goes_onto_the_bus.py.
answers.traces_to: Outline 11.3.2 and 11.4.2 (the device names on the command line); Law 7 (the diagnostic surface names the real lack, and 'no such device' for a declared device is the wrong one).
answers.what: bin/cairn maps a typed word to the folder whose charter declares it as answers_as whenever no class folder carries that word, even when instance-space holds a directory of that name, so cairn database and cairn inference keep resolving after their shims have run (outline 11.3.2, 11.4.2).

bullets.text: cairn inference / cairn database stop self-sealing: a declared answers_as now outranks the stray instance dir the shim itself writes.

title: bin/cairn maps a typed word to the folder whose charter declares it as answers_as whenever no class folder carries that
